payload.goal: Move sofar's hot path to a native Rust core without a big-bang rewrite: lock the black-box contract (SPEC plus a conformance suite over commands, hooks and record format), build sofar-core in Rust (hook handlers, event append, fold, digest/status render, statusline) behind the same CLI contract, integrate with TypeScript fallback, ship prebuilt per-platform binaries via npm, and prove it as its own benchmark arm; it ships only if no held-out lead margin shrinks (bench-refresh D19). After conformance parity, new hot-path code is Rust-only.

payload.because:
- Sofar runs on every tool call of every agent session. A native core gives near-zero hook start-up, fast folds over very large records (this repo's own is 9.7 MB), a single binary with no Node dependency for Codex/Cursor/OpenCode users, and headroom for many parallel agents.
- Measured 0.31 hooks are only ~0.75% of session time today, so the win is future scale and distribution rather than today's tokens. That is why it goes incrementally, and must pass the same benchmark gate as any other change.
- A conformance-first strangler port means neither implementation can drift from the SPEC.
payload.chose:
Adopt Rust for sofar's HOT PATH, incrementally, starting now. Ruled by the run owner 2026-09-15 ("yes do it").
SUPERSEDES, for the hot path only, the CLAUDE.md engineering conventions:
- "TypeScript strict mode; Node ≥18; ES modules";
- "Dependencies: … Nothing else without logging a Decision". Rust crates are limited to serde, serde_json and ulid until another Decision adds one.

Scope of `sofar-core`: hook handlers (session-start, user-prompt-submit, post-tool-use, stop, session-end), atomic event append, fold, digest/status render, and statusline.

TypeScript keeps: the MCP server, `sofar drive`, init/doctor/review, and cloud commands.

The contract comes first: docs/SPEC.md plus a black-box conformance suite over commands, hook stdin/stdout, env and record bytes. It runs against BOTH implementations.

The schema rail holds: event payload types stay authored ONLY in packages/schema/src. Rust types are GENERATED from them, never hand-written. Projection templates keep one source of truth, and Rust output is verified byte-identical by golden tests.

Parity gate: 100% conformance, perf targets met, and a benchmark arm "sofar-rust-core" vs "sofar-ts" that shrinks no D19 lead margin.

Sequencing: r1-fixes waves 1–2 land in TypeScript now, and the Rust core must reach parity INCLUDING them. After parity, new hot-path code is Rust-only, which stops the TypeScript port surface growing. Distribution: prebuilt per-platform binaries through npm optionalDependencies, with a TypeScript fallback.
payload.over:
- A big-bang rewrite now: it freezes waves 1–3, leaves round 2 unable to attribute gains, and means porting 27.6k engine lines and 34k test lines before anything is trustworthy.
- Staying TypeScript-only behind a measure-first gate: the run owner's point is that the port cost grows with every feature, and Codex CLI, Turborepo and Biome show the path is proven.
payload.rule: Hot-path event and projection behaviour is defined by docs/SPEC.md plus the conformance suite and must pass against both the TypeScript and Rust implementations; Rust schema types are generated from packages/schema/src, never hand-written.

plan.goal: Move sofar's hot path to a native Rust core incrementally (rust-core D1): contract first, then sofar-core in Rust behind the same CLI and hook contract, integrated with TypeScript fallback, shipped as prebuilt binaries, and proven as its own benchmark arm that shrinks no held-out lead margin (bench-refresh D19). After parity, new hot-path code is Rust-only.

Black-box conformance suite in the TS repo: runs an implementation binary against golden fixtures (real records including this repo's 9.7 MB log, calib and smoke cells, corrupt and unknown lines, concurrent appends) and compares stdout, exit codes and record bytes. Green on TypeScript first.
Perf baseline harness: hook p50/p95 cold start and fold/digest latency at 10, 100 and 1,000 initiatives and 1–10 MB records, TypeScript numbers recorded as the target to beat
Cargo workspace crates/sofar-core; schema codegen from packages/schema/src (no hand-written payload types); dependency list per D1
Event envelope and atomic O_APPEND append; unknown and corrupt lines skipped with a warning, never fatal, never rewritten
Fold to initiative state with conformance parity
Digest/status render byte-identical to the projection templates (golden tests), including the 10k char cap behaviour
Hook handlers (session-start, user-prompt-submit, post-tool-use, stop, session-end) with conformance parity, including r1-fixes wave 1–2 behaviour
Statusline command parity
TS entry points and hook shims dispatch to sofar-core when present, with TypeScript fallback and an explicit override for debugging
Prebuilt binaries per platform (darwin arm64/x64, linux x64/arm64, win32 x64) via npm optionalDependencies, plus a CI build matrix
Gate green: 100% conformance on both implementations and perf targets beaten
Benchmark arm sofar-rust-core vs sofar-ts under a frozen addendum; must shrink no D19 lead margin
Release after benchmark evidence (never before, per bench-refresh D20)
Switch the rule: new hot-path features are Rust-only; decide whether to port the remaining TypeScript surfaces

payload.because: The 10k injection cap, every clip budget, the redaction and guard regexes and the canonical event bytes all decide observable output; a Rust core that used its own defaults would pass no golden test against the live 9.4 MB record and would fork events.jsonl bytes on identical events (the spurious-diff hazard SPEC §Event envelope exists to prevent). Reproducing JS semantics is cheap and mechanical; tolerating drift would make "same bytes from both implementations" (D1) unprovable.
payload.chose: Byte parity is defined against the TypeScript engine's JavaScript text semantics, inventoried in docs/HOTPATH.md §Text-semantics pins: lengths and clips in UTF-16 code units, JS non-unicode regex classes, JS whitespace class, ECMAScript number formatting in canonical JSON, Node path.relative/basename, Math.round half-up, millisecond ISO timestamps. docs/HOTPATH.md is the hand-written contract inventory the conformance suite (1.2) drives; SPEC gaps it lists (G1–G15) are resolved by SPEC edits or Decisions, never by letting the two implementations differ.
payload.over: Rust-native defaults (char/byte lengths, Unicode-aware regex classes, ryu number formatting) with SPEC amended to tolerate the drift between implementations.
payload.rule: Hot-path Rust code reproduces the JavaScript text semantics pinned in docs/HOTPATH.md §Text-semantics pins, never Rust defaults; a parity difference is fixed in Rust or ruled by a Decision, never absorbed by loosening the conformance suite.

payload.because: Masking needs no hot-path code change in either implementation, keeps the shape of every volatile field asserted (a malformed ulid or timestamp still fails), and ulid randomness would defeat an unseeded clock override anyway. Leaving session-start's time-gated lines out would drop the surface the 10k cap and preface composition depend on.
payload.chose: The conformance suite (1.2) masks volatile bytes BY SHAPE instead of injecting a clock: a run-minted ulid becomes <ULID> only when its time part falls in the run's window, a run-minted ISO timestamp becomes <TS>, the two relative-age labels (Nm/Nh/Nd ago, ~Nh/~Nd since) become <AGO>, scratch paths become <ROOT>/<HOME>. Fixture bytes are never masked. Goldens are recorded from the TypeScript reference only, and only after the fixture horizon (newest fixture event + the 1 h cold-resume gap) so the presence of time-gated lines cannot flip. Everything else is pinned by building the child's environment from nothing but PATH (scratch HOME, git identity, XDG dirs, peer registry, update cache, LANG, TZ). Chosen under autonomy while the run owner's O6 ruling is outstanding; a SOFAR_NOW override can still be added later and would only shrink the mask list.

Latest stable 1.98.1 (2026-09-03); skip 1.98.0 (vtable miscompile); local machine has 1.97.1. x86_64-apple-darwin is Tier 2 since 1.90; aarch64-pc-windows-msvc Tier 1 since 1.91 (so ship win32-arm64 too, beyond the 3.2 list). (1.96) in tests; integer format_into/NumBuffer (1.98) for allocation-free digest rendering; std::io::pipe (1.87) if drive ever moves to Rust. Ideas only — adopting any of these that touches D1's crate list needs a Decision.

Rust research 2/6 — HOT-PATH ARCHITECTURE ideas. (1) Synchronous hook binary, no tokio. Have `sofar init` write hooks in exec form pointing at the RESOLVED native binary, never the npm .bin Node shim: one Node start per tool call is the main latency (esbuild overwrites its shim for the same reason). (2) Plain appends = build the full line, one write_all on O_APPEND. Check-then-append (lazy session registration) = exclusive File::lock on a SIDECAR `events.jsonl.lock` (Windows: append-only handles cannot be locked and LockFileEx may be mandatory — never lock events.jsonl itself); TypeScript must take the same lock (coordinate with r1-fixes 1.2 idempotent registration); add an idempotency key so the fold dedupes if a writer bypasses the lock; test N parallel MIXED Rust/TS writers (the 1.2 concurrent case is a natural home). (3) Incremental fold via a checkpoint {schema_hash, byte_offset, last_line_hash, state}: fold only the tail, any mismatch → full refold, partial last line skipped with a warning (maps onto the existing .index cursor rules in HOTPATH §Derived index on the hot path). (4) Byte-identity traps already pinned by HOTPATH P1–P9 and the 1.2 unicode/append goldens: 10k cap in UTF-16 units (len_utf16), sort by UTF-16 code units, JS `1e+21` vs ryu `1e21`, key order, serde_json REJECTS lone surrogates that JS accepts (syn.unicode append step has one), toISOString ms format, never localeCompare/Intl.

Rust research 3/6 — SCHEMA CODEGEN (task 2.1). Pipeline proposal: ts-json-schema-generator 2.9 → committed JSON Schema → typify 0.8 run from an xtask (not build.rs) → generated crate COMMITTED, with a CI regen-diff check. Pin the codegen to the TypeScript 5.9/6 programmatic API: TypeScript 7.0 has no stable programmatic API until 7.1 (this repo is on TS 7 — typescript-7 record). typify's anyOf handling is weak, so a narrow purpose-built emitter over the 37 exported schema types may be simpler than typify. guards.ts validation is LOGIC, not a type: port it by hand and conformance-test it separately (syn.guards golden).

Rust research 4/6 — CRATES. D1 currently allows serde, serde_json, ulid only; each addition below needs a Decision citing D1. Suggested: serde_json 1.0.151 on the hook path; lexopt for the hook CLI (clap only for a human CLI, if ever); insta (goldens), proptest, cargo-fuzz (fold must never panic on corrupt lines); gungraun + hyperfine for perf gates (1.3 harness); cargo-nextest. Keep tantivy, rmcp, tokio OUT of the hook binary. Optional and conditional: sonic-rs for bulk fold (needs compile-time SIMD; baseline x86_64 loses it), rkyv only as a versioned derived cache, memmap2 only for logs above ~10 MB (SIGBUS on truncation).

Rust research 5/6 — BUILD AND DISTRIBUTION (Phase 3). Release profile lto=fat, codegen-units=1, panic=abort, strip. PGO later via cargo-pgo on a replay corpus (the 1.2 fixtures are that corpus). Static musl on Linux. Per-platform npm optionalDependencies with a JS resolver that falls back to TypeScript when the native package is missing (npm/cli#4828 is the known optionalDependencies install bug). Provide an env switch between cores from the first integration (Turborepo lesson; matches 3.1's "explicit override for debugging"). Commit a pass/fail snapshot of conformance per platform (oxc pattern).

Rust research 6/6 — CAPABILITY EDGES to evaluate later (ideas, no decision): (a) Claude Code `mcp_tool` hook type could route PostToolUse to the already-running MCP server with no process spawn at all (not SessionStart; Codex/Cursor would still spawn). (b) napi-rs v3 can compile the same Rust to WASM so the TypeScript FALLBACK is the same core — conformance by construction, no dual maintenance (would change 3.1's fallback design). (c) Hash-chained log (blake3 per line + previous hash) → tamper-evident record, cheap cache validation, "state as of event N"; a FORMAT change, needs a FORMAT.md/SPEC Decision. (d) Offline BM25 search over 1,000+ records (tantivy or SQLite FTS5), outside the hook binary. (e) WASI 0.3 sandboxed user plugins (custom guards/renderers).

Rust research verdicts (peer session, 2026-09-15) 1/3 — for the run owner's review; nothing adopted, decisions still needed before use. ADOPT (no material loss found): toolchain 1.98.1 pinned via rust-toolchain.toml (skip 1.98.0); edition 2024 with let chains, cfg_select!, assert_matches!, format_into (MSRV only affects source builders; binaries ship); synchronous one-shot hook binary, no tokio; byte-identity trap fixtures (already in the 1.2 suite: UTF-16 cap, sort, number format, key order, surrogates, ISO ms); env switch between cores from day one; release profile lto=fat, codegen-units=1, panic=abort, strip, with split debuginfo kept for crash triage; static musl Linux; dev-only crates insta, proptest, cargo-fuzz, nextest, gungraun + hyperfine (dev deps, still listed in the D1 amendment).

Rust research verdicts 2/3 — ADOPT WITH A CONDITION (real pain found). File locking: Node has no native flock, so a Rust-only File::lock cannot coordinate with TypeScript writers; use a protocol both can implement (exclusive-create sidecar lockfile via open 'wx'/O_EXCL with stale-lock recovery) plus the idempotency key in fold; File::lock only once TS writers are gone; network filesystems stay best-effort. Direct native hook command: absolute machine-specific binary paths in a committed .claude/settings.json break teammates, CI and upgrades (npm prefixes differ); mitigate with a tiny sh/.cmd resolver shim (a few ms vs ~40 ms Node) or write paths only to settings.local.json, and keep a working default when the binary is absent. Incremental fold checkpoint: events.jsonl is NOT byte-append-only in practice — git union merges across branches/worktrees reorder or insert lines, so byte_offset alone is unsafe; validate with prefix hash + line count + last-line hash, any mismatch → full refold, fuzz it. Schema codegen (D1 requires it): ts-json-schema-generator pinned to TS 5.9/6; spike typify, fall back to a narrow emitter if unions come out poorly. Per-platform npm binaries: CI matrix and release complexity, Windows antivirus false positives, supply-chain signing — required to ship Rust at all, keep the TS fallback resolver. Claude Code mcp_tool hooks (no spawn): Claude-only, not at SessionStart, and capture silently stops if the MCP server is disconnected or crashed — only for non-critical capture, with missed-event detection, proven by ablation before relying on it.

Rust research verdicts 3/3 — DEFER (cost > gain today): napi-rs WASM single core replacing the TS fallback (WASM instantiate cost, no WASI flock, harder debugging; spike after Phase 2 parity, potentially a big maintenance win); tantivy search (multi-MB binary, index upkeep; `sofar find` exists; only on measured need, never in the hook binary); rmcp Rust MCP server (after parity, task 4.3); rkyv cache; memmap2 (SIGBUS, records under 10 MB); mimalloc (unproven for ms-lived processes); PGO (5–15% of a tiny runtime); WASI plugins (no product need yet); win32-arm64 (add when CI is stable). REDESIGN BEFORE CONSIDERING: hash-chained log — a single linear chain breaks under sofar's normal git union merges of concurrent branches/worktrees (two branches append different events, the merge interleaves them, the chain is invalid), plus corrections, export/import and old readers; if tamper-evidence is wanted, design per-session chains or a verification-time Merkle digest over ULID-sorted lines; needs a FORMAT.md/SPEC Decision. DECLINE: sonic-rs (compile-time SIMD, unchecked-UB APIs, slower on aarch64; serde_json suffices below ~10 MB).

payload.because: The user pays per spawn, so the measurement must include process start and be runnable against any implementation binary; per-cell p50 and p95 is the smallest set that catches both a median regression and a tail regression at each scale; hardware differences dwarf the margins being gated.
payload.chose: The perf target for the Rust core is the checked-in TypeScript baseline (packages/engine/test/conformance/perf/baseline.typescript.json), recorded by the 1.3 runner with the same black-box method the conformance suite uses (one process per hook, spawn to exit, p50/p95 nearest rank over 20 spawns) across 10/100/1,000 initiatives × 1/10 MB bound logs, this repo's record and a no-record floor. The 3.3 gate (SOFAR_PERF_GATE=1) passes only when every candidate p50 AND p95 is ≤ the target in every cell, candidate and reference re-measured on the same machine in the same sitting.
payload.over: In-process micro-benchmarks of fold/render (would not count node boot, the part Rust removes, and cannot run against a binary); a single aggregate score (would let a 10 MB regression hide behind a 1 MB win); comparing against numbers recorded on another machine.
payload.rule: A Rust perf claim is made only with `npm run perf` numbers (SOFAR_CONFORMANCE_BIN, same machine as a fresh reference run), never with in-process or hand-timed figures; the 3.3 gate is every cell's p50 and p95 at or under the recorded target.

payload.text: Hot-path perf: `npm run perf` (SOFAR_PERF=1 vitest --project perf, ~6 min, spawns ~1,200 processes) measures every hook, statusline and status at scale; `SOFAR_PERF_RECORD=1` re-records packages/engine/test/conformance/perf/baseline.typescript.json (+ .md), `SOFAR_PERF_CELLS=repo,floor` limits cells (merged into the baseline when recording), `SOFAR_CONFORMANCE_BIN=<binary>` measures a candidate with ratios, `SOFAR_PERF_GATE=1` fails a candidate over the target. Results for non-record runs land in $TMPDIR/sofar-perf.<impl>.{json,md}. Skipped under plain `npm test`. Never run it with other CPU-heavy work in flight — the numbers are wall clock.

1.3 baseline findings (Apple M4 Pro, node 24.15, a79c4a7; docs/HOTPATH.md §Perf baseline has the table). Boot floor is 31 ms per hook (node 21 ms + stub + fast bundle) — what a native binary removes. Fold cost scales with EVENT COUNT not bytes: 13 ms for 3,595 events, ~220 ms for 35,903, 2.3 ms for session-driver's 789 long lines; renderStatus < 1 ms. Appending hooks fold twice (handler + regenerateProjections) → ~610 ms vs ~313 ms read-only at 10 MB; sharing one fold is the first structural win (applies to TS too). The 100 ms shim budget holds only to ~1 MB/4k events; 10 MB blows it 3–6×. 1,000 siblings add ~70 ms warm / ~125 ms cold to session-start (registration scan + index rebuild), < 10 ms to other hooks. Rust improvement ideas from this (D3 record): (1) one fold per process shared by append and projections; (2) a streaming line decoder that validates the envelope without materialising a JSON value per line (serde borrowed structs); (3) the derived index as the primary read path for session-start's sibling scan so 1,000 siblings cost a directory listing, not 1,000 opens.

payload.text: 2.1 codegen findings (D3 record). (1) ts-json-schema-generator 2.9.0 installs its own TypeScript 5.9.3 nested under node_modules/ts-json-schema-generator, so the TS 7 workspace compiler is untouched — no separate package needed. (2) Rooting the schema at `KnownEventPayloads` (type: 'KnownEventPayloads', expose: 'export', topRef: true) pulls all 20 payloads, 5 nested objects and 7 string enums transitively, so no type list exists to drift; a vitest test asserts the registry has 20 members each referencing a *Payload definition. (3) `jsDoc: 'basic'` does NOT apply `@asType` annotations — 'extended' is required; it also copies TS doc comments into the JSON Schema and thence into Rust `#[doc]`, which is desirable (docs flow one way). (4) TS `number` → JSON `number` → typify `f64`, which cannot derive Eq and mis-states the four integer fields (threshold_pct, context_window, max_sessions, tokens); fixed at the schema home with `@asType integer` JSDoc tags so they generate as i64. Deriving Eq on every generated type is now a guard: a future `number` field without the tag fails the build. (5) typify 0.8 generates `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = Option::is_none)]` for optional fields and no deny_unknown_fields (schema emitted with additionalProperties: true), matching the TypeScript validators that ignore unknown keys. (6) Validation rules (conditional requirements, integer ranges) are logic and cannot come from the type schema — they are hand-ported in sofar-core (2.2/2.3) and proven by the syn.corrupt golden's exact warning text. (7) typify's xtask compiles in ~20 s cold; the regen check `cargo xtask schema --check` runs under `npm test` only when cargo is on PATH.

payload.because: D2 lets a parity difference be ruled rather than absorbed; the WTF-8 type would cost every string operation in the core for an input no real writer produces (JSON.stringify emits `\ud800` only when a JS string already held a lone half). The conformance case that carries one (repo.append step 12) goes through the TypeScript-owned `event append` and renders through `status` with the same U+FFFD bytes. Revisit with a WTF-8 type only if a golden ever shows a re-serialized lone surrogate.
payload.chose: The Rust core's JSON layer (crates/sofar-core/src/json.rs) reproduces JSON.parse/JSON.stringify semantics (P5: ECMAScript number formatting, last-wins duplicate keys, integer-like keys first in property order, f64 for every number, non-finite → null) with ONE ruled divergence: a lone-surrogate `\uD800`–`\uDFFF` escape decodes to U+FFFD at parse time, because Rust strings are UTF-8 and cannot hold a lone surrogate. UTF-16 lengths and stdout bytes are identical to Node's (which also emits U+FFFD when writing a lone surrogate); the only observable difference is a lone surrogate RE-SERIALIZED to JSON by the Rust core (`�` raw instead of `\ud800`), which can happen only when hook stdin or a log line carries one and the core re-emits it into an index file, a hookSpecificOutput line, or a payload it mints.
payload.over: A WTF-8 string newtype threaded through the fold, digest and every text helper so lone surrogates survive a round trip byte-for-byte; or serde_json::Value (rejects lone surrogates outright, u64/i64 number model, BTreeMap key order).
payload.rule: A lone-surrogate JSON escape decodes to U+FFFD in the Rust core; every other JSON.parse/JSON.stringify behaviour (P5) is reproduced exactly and proven by fixture tests generated from Node.

TASK CHANGES: (1) generator PARAMETERISED and exported (initiatives, writers, events per stream, type mix, size distribution with the tail) so the cloud harness drives the same one; (2) report the fold-cost CURVE vs events and vs bytes and name the log size that crosses 100 ms (≥100 ms refold p95 decides cloud refold-per-batch vs snapshot+tail); (3) always report COLD PROCESS and WARM FOLD separately; (4) digest and statusline render cost as one record's sessions[] grows to 100 writers; (5) union-merge test must include N branches appending to the SAME initiative's events.jsonl, plus across-initiative merges. 2.2 Rust improvement ideas recorded per D3 (none built): (1) a WTF-8 string type would remove the one ruled divergence (D13, lone surrogates) — worth it only if a golden ever shows a re-serialized lone surrogate. (2) `Object::js_ordered` reproduces JS property order (array-index keys first); if 2.4 finds no output that depends on insertion order, the Vec-backed object could become a sorted map for faster lookups on wide payloads (plan_updated). (3) `write_number` goes through `format!("{:e}")` — a direct shortest-digits routine (Ryu-style, via `core::fmt::flt2dec` if it stabilises) would remove an allocation per number; measure under D5 before touching. (4) `File::lock`/`try_lock` (std 1.89) stays out until the TypeScript writer is gone (D9); the O_EXCL sidecar via `File::create_new` (1.77) is what both sides share. (5) `Option::is_none_or` (1.82) and let-chains (edition 2024) carried the presence/absence semantics cleanly; `[T]::as_chunks` (1.88) in sha256. (6) identity: 2 s subprocess wait polls try_wait at 1 ms; a pipe-read with a deadline on a helper thread would cut the granularity if the ~8 ms git spawn is ever attacked (needs its own Decision per D7/O3). (7) `format_into` (named in the 2.2 next action) is not a std method at 1.98.1 — `std::fmt::Write` on String is the tool; no change needed.

payload.text: 2.3 design notes and improvement ideas (D3). Rust docs consulted: releases.rs 1.96–1.98 — assert_matches! (1.96), integer format_into / NumBuffer, str::substr_range, String::from_utf16le_lossy (1.98); none changes the hot path today. Ideas recorded, not built: (i) `format_into` for the `line N:` warning prefixes and the counters in to_json would drop one String alloc per warning — measure under 1.5 before adopting; (ii) the guard matcher memoizes failed (token, unit) states in a HashSet per pattern per subject — a bitset sized tokens×units would be allocation-free for the common short subject; (iii) state→Json→text for the `fold` output allocates the whole Json tree; a direct writer (as serialize_event does) would halve the canonical-output cost, but `fold` is a conformance surface, not a hook, so it does not gate 3.3; (iv) the snapshot wire is JSON-shaped exactly like the TypeScript SnapshotWire (same keys, insertion order per interface) — byte parity with TS was NOT made a goal because TS key order in `sessions[]` depends on event order (keys appear when first assigned); if 3.1 ever wants Rust to read a TS-written snapshot, parse_snapshot already accepts it shape-wise but the version check ties a snapshot to one engine version, so cross-implementation reading is a decision for later, not a bug. Known non-parity outside the contract: `--take`/`--since` accept JS Number forms for decimal/exponent/whitespace but not hex (`0x10`) — commander+Number would; the runner passes plain integers. Guards: no regex crate (D9) — the glob is compiled to the regex's automaton over UTF-16 units, `.` excluding the four JS line terminators (P3), and the guards.test.ts assertions are ported verbatim plus code-unit and line-terminator cases.

Fold parity against the Rust core: `cargo build --release -p sofar-core && SOFAR_CONFORMANCE_BIN="$PWD/target/release/sofar-core" npx vitest run fold-parity` (the runner splits the value on spaces, so use an absolute path with none; needs `npm run build` first for the reference in record mode only). The same eight cases run in-process with `cargo test -p sofar-core --test fold_parity`, which fails with a byte diff against golden/*.state.json. `npm run schema:emit` now runs BOTH emitters (fingerprint then Rust JSON Schema); a schema change means schema:emit, then `cargo xtask schema`, then a bumped snapshot version by construction (the fingerprint hash is baked at compile time via include_str!, the engine version via build.rs from packages/engine/package.json).

Peer sofar-r1-fixes-1c (2026-09-16, r1-fixes 2.5, D24 — commit to follow, post-RC release, NOT in 179b8fd which round 2 keeps measuring): three OPTIONAL fold outputs and one edge kind, additive, nothing renamed (D21), no golden changes. (1) `ran` edge gains attrs {ok, exit?, test?} ONLY when command_run carries `ok` (self-improve D2); `test` = the test-shaped shell segment per the closed recognizer in core/derived.ts (npm/pnpm/yarn/bun test, npx/bunx vitest|jest|mocha|ava|tap|pytest|rspec|phpunit|cypress run|playwright test|node --test, cargo/go/dotnet/swift/mix/gradle/mvn/make/deno/zig test; segments split on && || ; | newline, quote-aware, after VAR=value prefixes; clipped to 120 chars). (2) New edge kind `tested` (task → command:<event id>) for every task ACTIVE at a test-shaped command with a KNOWN `ok` — same window as `worked`; not in stateOf. (3) stateOf gains `sessions[].activity.failed?` (count of ok:false, absent when 0), `sessions[].activity.last_test?: {cmd, ok, exit?}`, `task_tests?: Record<taskId, {cmd, ok, exit?, ts, event_id}>` (absent when empty). Unknown `ok` is never a failure nor a test outcome. A record without `ok` folds byte-identically. Rust mirror: a follow-up to 2.3 once the r1-fixes commit lands and is merged here — port the recognizer (P3 regex semantics, quote-aware split) into fold.rs/edges_for_event + activity, extend GraphEdge attrs and SessionActivity/task_tests in to_json/from_json, and take the shared case (proposed id FP-09-command-outcomes-and-tests) into tests/fold_parity.rs. Not a 3.3 gate change: round 2 measures 179b8fd.

payload.text: Ideas from 2.5/2.6 (D3), none built: (1) every hook folds the bound log from scratch (fold_file) — the TypeScript engine caches per process only, so parity holds, but a per-record fold snapshot on disk (D14's versioned snapshot, keyed by log size+mtime like the index cursors) would make session-start/user-prompt O(new events) on the 9.7 MB record; measure under D5 at 1.5's corpus first. (2) refresh_guards and refresh_files each re-read graph.json/guards.json and re-run the pass; post-tool calls guards then (on a path hit) files, session-start calls both — one pass over both reducers would halve the meta reads. payload.because: Exit 64 is already the contract HOTPATH pins for "not mine" and D14 chose it precisely because the shim cannot know the colour ladder outcome; one env marker keeps both diagnostics for a human running sofar-core directly while the stub's fallback is the answer under dispatch. Sharing update-cache.ts between the stub and update-check.ts keeps one refresh policy, and the stub's cost is a file read only after a core-rendered statusline or status. The unfiltered run is the standalone 3.1 proof the plan asked for and is the shape the 3.3 gate and the 4.1 arm will use.
payload.chose: The boot stub (cli/boot.ts, rust-core 3.1) dispatches by exit code, not by re-parsing argv: every `event`, `statusline` and `status` argv is spawned on the native core with stdio inherited and `SOFAR_CORE_DISPATCHED=1`; the core's exit 64 (NotOurs, or a styled `status`) means "run the TypeScript CLI on the same argv" — the core reads no stdin before deciding and prints no exit-64 diagnostic when dispatched, so the fallback sees whole stdin and clean streams — and every other exit is mirrored. The core is `SOFAR_CORE=<path>` (`0`/empty forbids one), else the platform package `@sofar/core-<platform>-<arch>` resolved from the stub (the one constant 3.2 may rename); absent means TypeScript silently, a named core that cannot spawn warns once and falls back, a signal-killed core exits 1 (stdin gone, no fallback). The update-refresh claim moves to the stub after a core-rendered `statusline`/`status` (cli/update-cache.ts, node builtins only, shared with update-check.ts), keeping the O2 ruling that the binary only reads the cache; `sofar-core status` renders the stderr notice with the stderr caps ladder. Proof: the reference conformance suite with `SOFAR_CORE=$PWD/target/release/sofar-core` — 27/27 cases, no tag skipped, `event append`, styled `status` and `commit-trailer` reaching TypeScript through the stub's own fallback — plus a fake-core dispatch test under `npm test` and a negative control (a core that always exits 1 fails 25/27). The hook shims keep `exec sofar event <hook>`: a direct exec needs a stable per-machine binary path, which is the 3.2 install layout's to settle.
payload.over: The stub re-implementing the argv grammar (a third copy of parseRoot/dispatch) or the colour ladder to decide the styled-status case itself; capturing the core's stderr to hide the exit-64 diagnostics (changes the child's stderr TTY-ness, so a human at a terminal would get a plain notice where TypeScript colours it); the core claiming and spawning the refresh itself (O2, rejected); rewriting the shims to exec the binary now with an install path guessed ahead of 3.2.
payload.rule: The boot stub interprets exactly one core exit code, 64, as "TypeScript runs it"; the core never reads stdin or writes a byte before returning 64, and a new dispatched shape or a second interpreted exit needs a Decision citing this one.

payload.text:
Hook contract change from agents-parity 2.1 (D5, branch agents-parity, not yet on r1-fixes). It bears on rust-core 1.1, 2.5 and 3.1, and on memory-lead 1.4's hook mirror.

(1) Flag: every `sofar event <hook>` subcommand takes `--host codex`, in either `--host codex` or `--host=codex` form. The hot path (cli/fast.ts parseHookFlags) must accept it beside `--root`. Any other host value falls through to commander, which exits 1.

(2) Session identity: a declared Codex call registers its session as tool `codex`. Diagnostics host is `{tool:"codex"}`.

(3) Output: session-start and user-prompt stdout become `{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"SessionStart"|"UserPromptSubmit","additionalContext":<trimmed text>}}`. post-tool, stop and session-end pass through.

(4) Post-tool classification is now a list, not one call. `apply_patch` (tool_input.command holds the patch) appends one file_touched per `*** Add/Update/Delete File:` header: Add is write, Update is edit, Delete is delete. An Update followed by `*** Move to:` records delete on the source and write on the destination. Paths resolve against payload cwd. The session registers once; there is one diagnostics row per call, from the first classified subject.

payload.text: CI `test` job root cause (2026-09-21): every rust-core push since 3a284e6 hung in `npm test` until GitHub's 6h job limit cancelled it (runs 35201334756..35212040877; core matrix and core-conformance were green). The one file that never reported is packages/engine/test/update-check.test.ts: its 'survives a state dir it cannot write' case set XDG_STATE_HOME=/proc/definitely-not-writable, and on Linux mkdirSync({recursive:true}) under /proc gets ENOENT for the child and EEXIST for /proc and retries forever — a synchronous loop no vitest timeout can interrupt. Reproduced in Docker node:20 and node:24 (never returns); macOS throws at once, so it only shows on Linux. Fix: the unwritable state dir is a path under a regular file (ENOTDIR at once on every platform, as root too). main carries the same test but has no CI workflow, so the hang is latent there; it lands on main with the rust-core merge. Diagnosis method: vitest prints a file only when it finishes, so diff the files the CI log reported against `git ls-files '*.test.ts'` to find the one still running.

A vitest run that hangs in CI with no failure (job cancelled at the 6h limit) is a file that never finished: vitest prints a file's results only on completion, so diff the files the CI log reported against `git ls-files '*.test.ts'`. Never point a test's "unwritable" path under /proc: on Linux, mkdirSync({recursive:true}) there loops forever (ENOENT/EEXIST retry), a sync spin no test timeout can interrupt; use a path under a regular file (ENOTDIR on every platform, even as root). Reproduce Linux-only behaviour locally with Docker (`open -a Docker`, then node:20 / node:24 images).

payload.text: rc.2 re-pin done 2026-09-21, a day early: sofar-c3 reported the tag v0.33.0-rc.2 (cf8c117) existed. I merged it into rust-core. It brought 11 commits: the fold change 4d21c26, the drive --verify flags, the AGENTS.md block, and the version bump. Re-recording on Node 24 moved only the version in argv.fast-path and open.O2-update-segment. The other 25 goldens and every synthetic fixture came back byte-identical, which proves 4d21c26 changes no behaviour. sofar.sh's optionalDependencies, the five platform packages and package-lock.json now pin rc.2 (M7 procedure; `emit.mjs --check` passes, and `npm ci --dry-run` accepts the lock). The Rust fold had the same O(events × sessions) scan at six sites (record_freshness on every event, plus the session_started, session_ended, session_closed and handoff lookups). It is mirrored as fold::SessionIndex: a HashMap over the vec's tail, kept on FoldCheckpoint, never serialized, and exact because sessions are push-only. It has a unit test against a linear scan. Direct mode fails the same 11 hand-back cases with and without the mirror (D29/D31). D3 improvement idea, not built: the fold's id-keyed maps (SessionIndex, guard_cache, the activity accumulator) use std's SipHash. A std-only FxHash-style BuildHasher, with no crate under D9, could cut hashing cost on 10k+ sessions. Measure before adopting.

payload.text:
Hook contract change from agents-parity 2.1 (D5, branch agents-parity, not yet on r1-fixes). It bears on rust-core 1.1, 2.5 and 3.1, and on memory-lead 1.4's hook mirror.

(1) Flag: every `sofar event <hook>` subcommand takes `--host codex`, in either `--host codex` or `--host=codex` form. The hot path (cli/fast.ts parseHookFlags) must accept it beside `--root`. Any other host value falls through to commander, which exits 1.

(2) Session identity: a declared Codex call registers its session as tool `codex`. Diagnostics host is `{tool:"codex"}`.

(3) Output: session-start and user-prompt stdout become `{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"SessionStart"|"UserPromptSubmit","additionalContext":<trimmed text>}}`. post-tool, stop and session-end pass through.

(4) Post-tool classification is now a list, not one call. `apply_patch` (tool_input.command holds the patch) appends one file_touched per `*** Add/Update/Delete File:` header: Add is write, Update is edit, Delete is delete. An Update followed by `*** Move to:` records delete on the source and write on the destination. Paths resolve against payload cwd. The session registers once; there is one diagnostics row per call, from the first classified subject.

(5) Codex PostToolUse fires after non-zero exits too, so command_run and file_touched omit `ok` unless tool_response reports interrupted or timed_out; the diagnostics row gets `ok:null`.

(6) Codex shims: `.codex/hooks/sofar/{session-start,user-prompt-submit,post-tool-use,stop,session-end}.sh`, each running `exec sofar event <hook> --host codex --root "$(dirname "$0")/../../.."`. `.codex/hooks.json` runs them by git-root path.

Tests: packages/engine/test/codex-host.test.ts, against test/fixtures/codex/. SPEC: §Codex host, the "Wired" paragraph.

payload.text: sofar_update_plan (plan_updated) rebuilds the phase objects, so every phase NOTE set by an earlier phase_status_changed is silently dropped. The fold warns only about task and phase STATUSES, and the plan schema has no field to restate a note. After any plan replacement, re-issue sofar_update_phase with the same status and note for each phase that had one. To write to a record that lives on another worktree's branch (e.g. rust-core in ~/IO/sofar-rust-core) from a session whose MCP server is bound to main, spawn `sofar mcp` with cwd set to that worktree and call the tools over stdio JSON-RPC (initialize, notifications/initialized, tools/call). A plan_updated from main's stale copy would clobber the branch plan on union. Event-only writes (notes, memories, session events) can instead go through main and be carried over with `sofar export <slug>` | `sofar import - <slug> --root <worktree>`, which dedupes by id.

1.5 results, 2026-09-21 at c52db84 (rc.2 plus SessionIndex), one sitting, interleaved per D12, load 2.9 to 5.2. Filed as perf/team100.c52db84.{typescript,sofar-core}.* and perf/sessionindex.c52db84-vs-da1ae8b.*, and written up in the perf README and HOTPATH.md §Team scale. Writer cells (19 MB, ~27.8k events, ~1,740 sessions, 10 to 100 writers): the core is 0.61–0.82× of node p50 on every hook, with RSS 247–402 MB against 375–548 MB; writer count changes nothing at a fixed event count. The team100 cell (95.6 MB bound, 138,950 events, 8,576 sessions): 0.60–0.69× on append and read hooks, but session-start is 1.02–1.03× (4.67 s against 4.56 s warm), and the core's RSS of 1.25–1.75 GB is above node's 1.13–1.46 GB. Both folds are super-linear: 5.8 to 26 µs per event (TypeScript in-process) and 9.5 to 21 µs (core process) from 2.8k to 139k events. The TypeScript fold crosses 100 ms at ~13.2k events (9.1 MB) and 250 ms at ~25.7k (17.7 MB). The growth budget is 163 events and 0.11 MB per user per week, so at 100 users the hottest initiative crosses those lines in about 3 and 6 weeks. SessionIndex claim (D5/D12 satisfied, ABAB n = 25, load 4.4 to 3.2): the core with it is 0.81–0.92× p50 of the core without it on all 8 hooks at 10 MB and ~1,400 sessions, 25–35 ms per hook. Harness: the perf project's testTimeout goes to 60 min, because the interleaved team100 cell alone runs ~35 min.

IDEA (rust-core 1.5 turn 1, not built): files_touched membership is a linear scan per file_touched event, `includes` in fold.ts's applyEvent and `Vec::contains` at fold.rs's file_touched arm. The team100 corpus touches 60,686 distinct paths in 67,901 file events, so the fold is O(file events × paths). Measured share on the 95.6 MB log: TypeScript replayOne self time 2.9 of 4.2 s (applyEvent inlined, GC 0.1 s), and core apply_event plus memcmp ~940 of replay_one's ~1,300 samples, i.e. ~70% in both. Fix: an insertion-ordered set beside the array. It is behaviour-identical (order and first occurrence kept, no golden moves). Land it in TypeScript first (rust-core D1, likely an r1-fixes rc.3 item), then mirror it. Predicted: the team100 fold 3.6 s → ~1.1 s (TypeScript) and 2.9 s → ~0.9 s (core), per-event cost flat at ~6–10 µs, every team100 hook −60%, and about −40% at 19 MB. The biggest and cheapest of the four.

IDEA (rust-core 1.5 turn 2, not built): memory high-water in the core. It decodes every line into an owned JSON tree and holds all of them for the id-ordered replay (replay_decoded takes the whole DecodedLog), which is 13–18× the log's bytes: 1.25–1.75 GB RSS at 95.6 MB, above node's 1.13–1.46 GB. malloc and free are ~20% of the fold's samples. Idea: parse into values that borrow from the file buffer, and replay as a stream when the log is already in id order (append-only ULIDs almost always are), taking the voided set from a cheap first pass. Predicted: RSS ~2–3× the log (~250–300 MB at 95.6 MB), and 15–20% off the fold. A team machine with several agents open pays this per concurrent hook.

IDEA (rust-core 1.5 turn 3, not built): session-start does not win at team scale (core 1.02–1.03× of node on team100, warm and cold). A cold-index sample puts 1,675 of handle_session_start's 2,147 samples in index_tier1::refresh_file_states, the derived index's tail read over the siblings' 345 MB. The warm path still pays the bound fold (with turn 1's scan) plus ~1.7 s the sample did not isolate. Idea: profile the WARM path after turn 1 lands, before designing anything. Predicted: turn 1 alone takes ~2 s off the 4.7 s warm start. Matters for 4.1: the benchmark arm's session-start at team scale is not a core win today.

IDEA (rust-core 1.5 turn 4, not built; needs a Decision citing r1-fixes D20): every hook refolds the whole log. The incremental-fold snapshot (r1-fixes 5.1, D20–D22) is a consumer API that the engine never persists under .sofar/, so a hook on a 139k-event log replays all of it every time (2.6–4.7 s per warm hook at team100). Idea: a per-clone persisted checkpoint in the state directory ($XDG_STATE_HOME/sofar, never .sofar/, so still derived and never synced), validated by cursor and refused by D22's closed set, with hooks replaying only the tail. Predicted: warm hooks from seconds to roughly snapshot load plus render (~0.1–0.3 s at team100), which removes the growth-budget cliff (the hottest initiative crossing 100 ms in ~3 weeks at 100 users) instead of moving it.

payload.text:
1.5 turn 3, profiled 2026-09-22 before anything was designed, as HOTPATH asks. The prediction below is written BEFORE the build (bench-refresh D10).
- A warm session-start at team100 takes 3.54 s at 8bad310. A sample puts 2,159 of its 3,144 samples in index_tier1::refresh_file_states -> index_store::read_index_file -> json::parse of `.sofar/.index/graph.json` (28.8 MB). That is ~2.1 s, about 14 MB/s.
- The cause is json::Object::insert, which scans linearly for a duplicate key, so parsing an object with K keys is O(K^2). graph.json's `initiatives.<slug>.files` objects hold 60,691 keys (the bound initiative), then 32,012, 21,842, 16,645 and so on: ~1.8e9 key compares. TypeScript's JSON.parse is hashed, so this cost exists only in the core, and it is fixed there directly (the decision logged earlier this session).
- Also at session_start.rs:424: 901 samples, the bound fold.
- Fix: the parser dedupes through a key->index HashMap once an object passes a small size, and keeps JSON.parse semantics: the last value wins, at the first occurrence's position. Object::get stays linear. Behaviour is unchanged.
- PREDICTED: warm session-start at team100 from ~3.3 s to ~1.3 s (-2.0 s, ~0.4x). Cold start about -2 s of its ~7 s (~0.7x), since its tier-1 build also parses. At 19 MB, where files objects hold ~12k keys, a smaller share: warm ~0.85x. Other hooks do not read graph.json and stay flat. Measured with its own interleaved arm against 8bad310.

MIRROR OWED at the next RC re-pin: drive-visibility 2.2 (be4ce88, on main after rc.2) changed the fold. Reported by peer sofar-1b on 2026-09-22; the reasoning is in drive-visibility D8 and its 2.2 task note.
- New event `run_adopted {run, epoch}`. The validator rejects epoch < 2 (run_started is epoch 1). An adoption for a run that never started is skipped with the warning `adoption of run "<id>" that never started — skipped`.
- RunState gains `adoptions: [{id, ts, epoch}]` in replay order, and `owner: {id, epoch}`. The owner starts as run_started's own event id at epoch 1. Only a STRICTLY higher epoch takes it; replay is in id order, so on a tie the first id keeps it.
- `stop_requests` now holds EVENT IDS instead of envelope timestamps; the property name is unchanged.
- run_adopted is excluded from drift, like the other driver events (record_freshness's driver list).
- Fold-parity: new case FP-11-run-adoption-fencing. The FP-06 golden and schema-fingerprint.txt are regenerated. SCHEMA_VERSION is unchanged. D21: never rename the new case id.
- describeRun, if the core renders it: `, resumed (epoch N)` after the policy once owner.epoch > 1, and "stop requested" counts only requests whose id sorts after owner.id.
- Together with typed-judge 4.1/5.1 (note 01M341T4), this is the rc.3 re-pin's scope so far. Until then the core matches rc.2, and the stub must not dispatch it under a newer engine.

The port cost also grows with every batched commit. D11's rule stands: every target still names its TypeScript commit. Only the cadence changes, from RC tags to trunk.

It prints only when the line minus its liveness word differs from the session's mark in <state base>/drive-seen/<clone key>.json (version 1, {marks: {<session>: {seen, seq}}}, cap 64, written only on news), probes the run lock only when it prints, and is silent when SOFAR_DRIVE_NUDGE is set. Mirror owed, reported by peer sofar-3c on 2026-09-22: drive-visibility 3.3, the statusline drive segment (ce2f9f2 on main, unpushed when reported). After the record's progress the segment reads `drive <task>` (lock held; `running` when nothing is queued), `drive <task> liveness unknown` (no lock here), `drive gone` (lock free, no stop), or `drive <reason>` (a stop since the session began; nothing when the session is unknown). The label is dim; the value is toned (task cyan, gone red, needs_user yellow, error/stall red, closed green, other reasons dim). The pure core to mirror is statusline.ts driveSegmentOf(state, sessionStarted, probe), and the lock is probed only while a run is open. The task comes from core/drive-queue.ts nextTask, as for 3.2's prompt drive line (d049068). It joins the next trunk merge (rust-core D29).

File-mention cross-check against the TypeScript extractor (memory-lead 2.1 mirror): bundle a script that imports packages/engine/src/core/file-mentions and writes one JSON line per decision/note text found in every .sofar/initiatives/*/events.jsonl, as {text, mentions, depths} with depths against /repo/src/core/fold.ts. Then run `SOFAR_MENTIONS_PAIRS=<jsonl> cargo test -p sofar-core --test mentions_crosscheck -- --ignored`. Ignored by default. Run it whenever file_mentions.rs or core/file-mentions.ts changes. It passed on 1,238 texts at main a4f270a.

After merging main into rust-core, generated record files (.sofar/**/*.md) often conflict, and events.jsonl never does (merge=union). Take either side with `git checkout --ours -- <paths>`, then regenerate from the union-merged log. `sofar import` re-projects only when it appends something, so it cannot do this. Instead, esbuild-bundle a 4-line script that calls createToolContext(root).foldState(slug) and regenerateProjections(ctx.initiativeDir(slug), state) from packages/engine/src, and run it with the root and slugs. Before committing, check `grep -c '^<<<<<<<' events.jsonl` is 0: several logs hold literal conflict markers inside note payloads, which are not conflicts.

Conformance cases that need files outside the fixture's dot-sofar use the step's `before: (m) => …` hook (m.root, m.home). syn.surfacing writes source files and a check-approval trust file at <home>/.local/state/sofar/checks/<sha256(realpath(root/.git))[:32]>.json with approved[sha256(cmd)]. syn.copies fakes linked worktrees under m.home: <root>/.git/worktrees/<n>/{gitdir,HEAD,commondir} plus <home>/<n>/.git. They go under m.home so the goldens tildify them to ~/<n>. Scratch paths outside root and home are not masked and would make the golden machine-specific.

2.11 status, 2026-09-23 (5809bc1, 5d07c19 and 5ddb5d7 on rust-core, unpushed).
BUILT: the lexicon tier, indexed_lessons and prompt_lessons in the core, byte-compatible with 3ee5e98. Conformance cases repo.lessons and syn.lessons-cut were recorded from the TypeScript reference. All 32 goldens pass through the stub, and both new cases pass with the core standalone. Hand interop on the repo fixture: a tier built by one implementation and extended by the other is byte-identical to a single-implementation run, in both orders.
MATH.LOG, BOUNDED: V8's Math.log is fdlibm with FMA fusion on arm64. f64::ln differed from it in the last bit on 4.2% of 1M BM25 inputs, so the fold-path rank_lexicon in the core was already an ulp off. It NEVER SHIPPED: the sofar-core-<platform> packages have never been published (they 404 at every version), so the native core has never reached a user. It is an EXACTNESS bug, not a ranking-quality one. An ulp moves a ranking only where two scores sit within an ulp, or where a score sits on a cut, and syn.lessons-cut builds exactly that case. Fixed by js_math.rs (decision 01M35KRH, HOTPATH P10).
OPEN, and what closes it: (1) the ci.yml js_log crosscheck must pass on all five core-matrix targets. The x86-64 unfused variant is inferred and unproven locally: this Mac has no Rosetta, and ubuntu-24.04-arm is built with gcc, which may fuse differently from clang. (2) D18 for the Rust tier: read-path p50 on a quiet host, lid open, with a cold first run checked explicitly (sofar-c3: TypeScript's cold cost was session-start +2.9 ms and statusline +2.4 ms; rc.1's warm gate was +0.5 to +1.2%). 2.11 stays active until both land.

D3 improvement ideas from 2.11 (none built): (1) The prompt hook parses the whole lexicon.json every prompt. Its `docs` strings are the bulk of it, and only slugs with a hit need decoding, so a lazy per-slug decode or a byte-offset table would cut the warm read at team100. Measure first. (2) postings_map and postings_text rebuild a HashMap and sort it for every touched bucket on every write. A merge of sorted term lines would be linear, but the write only runs when a decision, note or stall arrives. (3) Every write rewrites all 33 shard files, because each carries the gen. A per-shard gen checked against a gen vector in the table would let a write touch only the buckets it changed. That is a format change, so it needs a TypeScript-first decision in memory-lead, and the core must not diverge on its own. (4) LexiconIndex reads a shard at most once per prompt; that already matches the TypeScript and needs no change.

payload.text: Writing a record whose truth is on another worktree's branch: rust-core lives in ~/IO/sofar-rust-core, and main's copy of it is stale. Event-only writes (notes, decisions, memories, session events) may go through main; carry them over with `sofar export <slug>` | `sofar import - <slug> --root <worktree>`, which dedupes by id. Better still, append them in the worktree itself: `node packages/engine/dist/cli.js event append <slug> --session <id> --type <type> --payload -`, which also avoids the rebinding in rust-core M17. A plan replacement (plan_updated) must be made on the branch, by spawning `sofar mcp` with that worktree as cwd: from main's stale copy it clobbers the branch plan when the copies union. task_added and task_status_changed need no plan replacement and can be appended in the worktree the same way.

sofar_update_plan (plan_updated) is a full replace that silently drops every phase NOTE; the plan schema has no field for it. Snapshot and diff around every call, per self-improve M8: copy .sofar/initiatives/<slug>/plan.md aside before, diff after, and restore anything lost with sofar_update_phase (the phase name, status and note verbatim). This replaces the old advice to remember to re-issue sofar_update_phase, which failed twice in one night on 2026-09-22.

payload.text:
4.4 profile and in-process work, 2026-09-23 ~20:20-21:00 IST. CONDITION: UNDER LOAD from the Chain L author's session (load 2.8-4.4). All timings are relative and interleaved, for locating cost only. Per sofar-e8's hold, none is a claim or a gate (D5, D12).
Corpus: team100, bound log 95.6 MB / 138,950 events (a clone of 312c2620's prof corpus). Every hook replays the whole log per process. At efdbf68 the read hooks took 1.0-1.3 s and post-tool 1.5 s.
Landed on rust-core, all exact. Evidence: the team100 folds (21 logs) are byte-identical to efdbf68's, conformance 32/32, fold-parity + real-logs 248/248, render parity, clippy clean.
- 6aa6c77: split_segments returns slices, and lit no longer copies its word.
- acde2fe: finalize_state reads the edges in place. finalize_fold cloned the edges and fold_state then dropped them, ~20% of statusline. registered() asks the checkpoint's SessionIndex without finalizing.
- 1dd6083: the test matcher reads a four-word window, and activity looks up before allocating.
Relative results against efdbf68 (n=7): read hooks -19 to -25%, post-tool -34%. 1dd6083 alone is -2 to -3%, which is noise.
WHAT REMAINS at acde2fe, statusline (520 samples): replay 58% (decode + JSON parse ~35%, test_shaped_command ~16%, format! ~9%), finalize_state 22%. Both are proportional to the log, so no in-process change reaches 20 ms at team100. Reading 95 MB alone costs a large share of that.
THE STRUCTURAL CHOICE, which needs the operator:
(A) Persist a snapshot (D14: versioned, outside the record) and apply only the tail per hook. This is bounded by parsing the snapshot (a ~24 MB state as JSON is ~100 ms with our parser) plus finalize (~100 ms), so it is likely 150-250 ms, not 20. A binary format would need a crate (D9). It also has to settle whether .sofar/.index counts as "outside the record" (D14, r1-fixes D20).
(B) Cache each read hook's output, keyed by the log's (size, mtime) and that hook's other inputs. This is the only in-process path to <20 ms, but each hook's inputs (git, clock, other records) have to be enumerated exactly. It is TS-first, since the behaviour is shared.
(C) A warm local process that holds the folds. This touches the "state server serves JSON on localhost" guard-rail.
Recommendation: (B) for statusline and user-prompt, whose inputs are narrow, plus (A) as the base for post-tool and session-start. Both are TS-first designs. Nothing is built until the operator rules.

Only skipping the fold entirely (B) can reach 20 ms, and it is safe only where a hook's inputs are narrow and can be enumerated. That is the home sync-client D2 and self-improve D3 already use, and it refuses any path that resolves inside the clone. No new rule and no guard-rail touched: no new crate (serde_json is in D9), no server, no sync. C (a warm process) is not chosen.
payload.over: (A) placed in .sofar/.index/, which is gitignored but under .sofar/, so SPEC's snapshot law forbids it. (B) keyed on the log alone, which goes stale when git, the clock or another record changes. One mechanism for all five hooks: A alone cannot reach 20 ms, because parse and finalize grow with the log, and B alone cannot serve an appending hook, whose output changes with every write. (C) a warm process, not chosen.

payload.text: D3 IDEA, unbuilt (per the operator ruling on 4.4, 2026-09-23): an edge-free hook checkpoint for the APPENDING hooks (post-tool, stop). As replay produces each GraphEdge, fold it straight into finalize's accumulators instead of keeping the edge: ActivityAcc per session, task_files per task, task_tests per task. It is exact, because task_files_from_edges, task_tests_from_edges and activity_from_edges are all left folds over edges in log order. It would persist ~25 MB at team100 against 265 MB with edges. Predicted gain: appending hooks ~1 s -> ~400 ms at team100. That is bounded by parsing ~25 MB (~10 ms/MB in the core) plus projection regeneration. Costs: a second checkpoint shape in both implementations, the fold-parity suite extended to it, and FoldResult.edges still needing the full replay wherever adjacency is read (find, graph). Never built without its own measurement and Decision.

payload.because: Session-start profile at team100 (2026-09-23, under load, relative): fold 316 of 523 samples, refresh_file_states 128 (index JSON parse 80), render_status 40 (open_session_file_conflicts 33), attribution 11. The options (repo memory, neighbours, rules, notices) take part in renderStatus's cap arithmetic, so the state part cannot be rendered once and composed. The only exact route that skips the fold is a smaller state that provably renders the same, and "provably" here means a byte-parity suite over real and synthetic records.
payload.chose: 4.4 B for session-start is a FACTS-level cache, not an output cache. Cache a trimmed "digest state" per record in .sofar/.index/digest/<slug>.json. It holds the finalized InitiativeState with every unbounded collection cut to exactly the members renderStatus and its helpers can reach: sessions (last with summary, last unwritten with activity, the unwritten list, open sessions, overlapping write-backs), with files_touched dropped. The key is the log's size + mtimeMs + engine + schema, and a miss folds and rewrites. Every live input (session id, git, repo memory, neighbours, rules, notices, env switches) stays live and is passed to renderStatus unchanged. The cut rule is enforced by a parity suite, not by argument: renderStatus(digestState(s), o) must equal renderStatus(s, o) byte for byte over every real log in this repo, the team100 corpus and the status fixtures, across a matrix of options. It runs in both implementations, TS first then the Rust mirror. The file-states index read (refresh_file_states, ~25% of session-start at team100) is the next cost after that. It belongs to record-index's index format, so it is named here and not changed.
payload.over: An output cache keyed by every input: it can never hit, because the output carries `Session: <id>`, session-start fires once per session, and the notices carry clock-derived ages. Also over caching the full edge-free state: 14 MB at team100 is ~140 ms to parse in the core.

SPIKE: edge-free fold checkpoint (per sofar-e8, never merged). Branch spike/edge-free-checkpoint, commit 15940fa, TS only. 2026-09-24 ~04:15 IST. Timings are RELATIVE and UNDER LOAD (load 4.8-5.1), TS in-process with no node boot.
DESIGN: finalize's three reducers (task_files, task_tests, per-session activity including each session's seen-path set) are left folds over edges, so the checkpoint persists their ACCUMULATORS instead of the edges. Resume = parse, then appendToCheckpoint for each tail line, then continue the three folds over the tail's edges, then finish. appendToCheckpoint's existing refusals (a correction, an out-of-order id, an undecodable line) fall back to a refold.
PARITY vs a full refold (JSON of the finalized state): this repo's real logs, every initiative, tails of 1 and 25: 116 OK, 2 REFUSED (felt-cost and sync-client at tail 25, the safe fallback), 0 DIFF. team100 bound log, tails 1/5/25/200: 4/4 OK.
SIZE: team100 25.6 MB (against 265 MB for the D22 snapshot with edges). Real records here: 0.02-0.20 MB.
TIME at team100 (TS): full fold 1305 ms. Resume = parse 52-58 ms + tail and finish 25-28 ms, so ~80 ms. Rewrite = serialize 33-56 ms + write 22-27 ms.
PER-HOOK estimates at team100 (TS): user-prompt ~80 ms resume + ~80 ms of its own extras. post-tool ~80 ms resume + append + projection regen + a checkpoint rewrite (~60-80 ms; amortize by rewriting every K appends or when the tail passes X bytes). Active statusline ~80 ms + facts. Node boot comes on top.
RUST CAVEAT: the core's own JSON parser runs ~10 ms/MB (the 265 MB snapshot took 2.6 s), so a 25 MB checkpoint is ~250 ms: 3x better than its refold, but slower than V8. A typed serde_json (serde and serde_json are already D9 crates) is the likely fix, still to measure.
BUILD ESTIMATE: TS: fold.ts accumulate/finish split (finalizeFold keeps its contract); a checkpoint store in the per-clone state dir (D34 placement: key = engine + schema + log prefix bytes, lines and last-line hash, as D22 does; atomic writes); resume wired into ctx.foldState; a post-tool rewrite policy; tests: fold-parity extended to the edge-free shape (snapshot+tail over the FP cases and real logs), stale/corrupt/concurrent fallback. ~5-7 files, ~700-900 lines with tests. Rust: the mirror in fold.rs, a store, the serde_json typed path, and parity: ~900-1,200 lines. About 2-3 focused sessions. Checkpoint files per implementation (tagged by engine) avoid a byte-parity burden on a 25 MB derived file.
OPTIONS:
(a) Build it. Active-session hooks at team100 drop from ~1 s to ~150-250 ms (user-prompt, post-tool, active statusline). It is the only option that moves them. Still not 20 ms at team100 while a session is active.
(b) Finish user-prompt B for the quiet case only. Small gain: active sessions miss.
(c) Stop 4.4 at what landed: session-start ~49 ms and statusline ~15 ms on a quiet log. Active hooks stay ~1 s at team100.
RECOMMENDATION: (a), and restate 4.4's target honestly: under 20 ms on quiet reads at team100 (met: session-start 49 ms is the one outlier to re-measure on the gate), and a bound for active-session hooks at team100 (e.g. <=250 ms), because 20 ms there needs a resident process, and C was rejected. The operator rules.

payload.text:
PROPOSAL (not built): dirty-only projection regeneration, for rust-core 4.4's appending hooks. Templates UNTOUCHED; only the scheduling changes.
WHY: an in-process post-tool profile at team100 puts regenerate_projections at 76%: write_if_changed reads back all 8,576 sessions/*.md on every append (65%), and rendering them is another 10%.
FACT: projections/templates/session.ts renderSession(state, session) reads only state.slug plus that one finalized SessionState (id, tool, model, started, ended, closed_reason, handoff, summary, next_action, activity). Its helpers (describeActivity, testOutcomeLine, doc) take session data only. plan.md, decisions.md and memory.md read much of the state, but they are three files.
DESIGN:
(1) Keep plan.md, decisions.md and memory.md exactly as today: render and write-if-changed on every regeneration.
(2) sessions/<id>.md: a session is DIRTY unless ALL of these hold: (a) the manifest holds its input fingerprint sha256(canonical JSON of {slug, the finalized SessionState}) and it equals the current one; (b) the file on disk still has the size and mtime the manifest recorded when it wrote it (a hand edit, deletion, restore or git checkout makes it dirty); (c) the manifest's key matches. A dirty session is rendered and written if changed exactly as today, then re-recorded. A clean session is neither rendered nor read.
(3) KEY, and a full rebuild when it moves: the engine version + schema hash + a PROJECTION FINGERPRINT, sha256 over the implementation's own template sources computed at BUILD time (TS: build.mjs hashes src/projections/templates/**; Rust: build.rs hashes its projections/status ports, as it already embeds the schema fingerprint). Any template edit, even within one version, changes the key, so every session is dirty. Where no fingerprint is available (TS run from source under vitest), everything is dirty, which is today's behaviour.
(4) The manifest is derived only: .sofar/.index/projections/<slug>.<impl>.json, atomic writes, a lost or corrupt file meaning every session dirty. Session files whose session no longer exists are left as today (the current generator never deletes).
PARITY TEST, which fails on any missed dirty file: replay each real log and team100's bound log event by event (and in batches). After each step, regenerate one tree with dirty scheduling and a second tree with the full generator, then compare the two directories byte for byte, all files. Plus cases for: a hand-edited session file, a deleted one, the slug changing, a template fingerprint change (full rebuild), and a corrupt manifest. Mutation checks: dropping slug from the fingerprint, skipping the on-disk size/mtime check, or ignoring the key must each turn it red. Both implementations, TS first, then the Rust mirror with the same test over the core.
EXPECTED: post-tool at team100 about 251 -> ~100 ms (relative). Hashing 8,576 small sessions costs a little; reading and rendering them goes away.
Needs: your go, and a Decision (it changes when projections are written, not what).

01M39M4B BUILT in both implementations (rust-core, unpushed): TS 7f804fa7, Rust 179be8f4. Byte-identical to a full regeneration at every step of an event-by-event replay (TS: every real log plus a team-shaped corpus; Rust: logs under 256 KB). The renderSession inputs are enforced (TS Proxy; Rust bare-state render). Hand-edit, delete, slug, fingerprint and corrupt-manifest cases pass; four mutations each go red in both implementations. Full npm 3161/0; cargo 162/0; conformance 32/32; fold-parity + real-logs 281/281; render parity. Relative, UNDER LOAD (~4.4-5): post-tool at team100 228 -> 192 ms (-16%), now inside the <=250 ms bound; user-prompt 92 ms and stop 63 ms unchanged. The prediction was ~100 ms; the gap is that dirty scheduling itself now costs: hashing 8,576 sessions per append (sha256 plus canonical JSON, ~63% of it) and stat-ing their files (~17%). Further lever, NOT built: hash only the sessions a tail can change. That needs its own exactness proof (which SessionState fields an event can move). An in-process post-tool profile at team100 (relative, under load, core 179be8f4, ~215 ms per call) puts regenerate_dirty_sessions at ~66% of the call: session_input_hash ~63% of that (sha256 967 samples plus canonical JSON ~770, over all 8,576 sessions per append), file stats ~17%, writes ~13%. Lever: hash and stat only the sessions a tail can change, i.e. those named by the tail events plus any a proven rule adds. Exact only after proving which SessionState fields an event can move (session_ended, activity, per-session unwritten drift, handoff). Predicted post-tool ~192 -> ~90 ms at team100. Never build it without that proof and a Decision.

PROPOSAL (not built): warm session-start at team100 against the <20 ms quiet-read bar. Current: 53.5 ms per call in-process (relative, core 179be8f4; the real process adds ~2 ms boot). Profile (1,971 samples):
- resolve_session_first -> home_initiative 26%: parses all 20 registration caches (2.75 MB) every call. The corpus's synthetic ts are older than the files' mtimes, so the mtime prune never fires.
- cached_digest_state 23%: the core's own Json parser on the 4.3 MB digest plus from_json.
- read_attribution_query -> run_git 21%: a git subprocess every call.
- render_status 18%: repo_rule_lines 11%, conflicts 3%, constraints 2%.
- refresh_guards 7%: a 1.1 MB guards index parse.
LEVERS, each exact:
L1 (TS first, then Rust; shared behaviour): cache the bounded attribution walk per HEAD sha. The walk is a pure function of the commit graph from HEAD for a fixed window, and a sha's ancestry is immutable. Derived file .sofar/.index/attribution.json {head sha, window, result}, where a different HEAD (readGitState already reads it without a subprocess) is a miss. Saves ~21%.
L2 (Rust only, formats unchanged): read the digest cache, registration caches and guards index with TYPED serde_json (D9 crates, as the checkpoint does) instead of the Json parser plus from_json. The bytes on disk and the TS side are untouched. Per the port-only-cost rule it is fixed in the core directly. Expected ~3-4x on those parses.
L3 (only if L1+L2 fall short; a D35 format change, so it needs its own Decision): shard each log's registration cache by a session-id hash prefix, as the lexicon shards are, so home_initiative parses 1/32 of it per log.
L4 (investigate): repo_rule_lines at 11% is likely a port-only ranking cost, to check against the TS reference.
ESTIMATE (relative): 53.5 -> ~42 ms after L1 -> ~22 ms after L2 -> ~18 ms after L4, with L3 as the margin. HONEST READ: 20 ms looks reachable WITHOUT a resident process, but only just. It rests on estimates, and each lever needs measuring. Order: L2 (Rust-internal, no format change), then L1 (TS first), then measure, then L4 and L3 only if needed.

payload.text: 4.4 L2 landed (f09e1fd6): the Rust core reads the digest, registration and index caches (guards via read_half/read_index_file) through json::parse_bytes_fast. serde_json's tokenizer builds the crate's Json (same key order and duplicate rules), and ANY rejection falls back to the crate parser, so invalid UTF-8 and lone surrogates keep D13. serde_json gains the float_roundtrip FEATURE (no new crate, D9): without it, mtime-shaped floats (e.g. 1790177657980.5837) round 1 ulp off. The differential test the_fast_parse_equals_the_parser (every real log line, every .index json, a 20k float sweep) fails when the feature is removed. Cache formats and writers are unchanged. Conformance, fold parity and render parity 210/210 via SOFAR_CORE; cargo 159. D3 idea, unbuilt: move the remaining derived-file reads (neighbours cache, session_pointer, drive_seen, statusline facts) to parse_bytes_fast.

4.4 L1 landed (4b5b62b2), per the standing rule. The SessionStart attribution walk is cached in .sofar/.index/attribution.json under the FULL HEAD sha (headSha, from files: a detached sha or a refs/heads tip from the common dir) plus maxCount. It is derived only; any mismatch, corrupt or mis-shaped file re-walks and rewrites. The walk passes the sha as its rev, so the cached answer is exactly the key's history, even if HEAD moves mid-walk. When no sha resolves from files, it walks uncached; a failed walk is never cached. TS first, Rust second, byte-identical files.

Parity is proven by packages/engine/test/attribution-cache.test.ts: output is identical cold, warm and under 11 corrupt variants, across a commit and a checkout that move HEAD. The Rust core reads the TS file and writes identical bytes. A forged-under-key control proves hits are trusted. Mutation checks (key without head; loose shape check) fail in both implementations. Full vitest 3166 passed.

Known limit, logged as a D3 idea: the key does not see a shallow-clone deepen or refs/replace at an unchanged HEAD.

payload.text: D2/D13 parity fix (c6781e21, P5 fixture c2b9dfbb). Rust's {:e} shortest formatting breaks an exact decimal tie the other way from JS: the double 1790271792402.78125 printed ...7813, while Number::toString (ECMA-262: the closest candidate, the even one on a tie) prints ...7812. Effect: the Rust core wrote a different mtimeMs into the digest cache than TypeScript for such mtimes, so a mixed install re-folded on cross-reads. It never rendered wrongly, but it broke byte parity. It predates 4.4 and is already on main. The rc.3 merge gate caught it: digest-cache's TS/Rust byte-identity test on a fresh checkout, whose new mtimes hit a tie. Fix: json::tie_to_even confirms the tie on the exact expansion and takes the even neighbour only if it round-trips. The tie cases joined the P5 Node fixture (crates/sofar-core/tests/fixtures/js-numbers.txt, 745 -> 1746 cases), so it cannot regress silently; mutation-checked. Also fixed for rc.3: 6d65ccf7 (the 4b quiet-read test no longer reads the derived .sofar/.index). The rc.3 gates now run cargo and vitest with .sofar/.index absent.

payload.because: The digest read is 43% of warm session-start at team100 (4.35 MB file; 8,576 sessions and 2,014 decisions mostly carried in full for rendering that never reads their text). The renderStatus(digestState(s)) === renderStatus(s) contract is already pinned over real logs and the options matrix, so a tighter cut stays exact. Estimated ~32 → ~20–21 ms, in both engines.
payload.chose: Tighten the digest cache cut, DIGEST_CACHE_VERSION 1 → 2 (D-b, operator ruling 2026-09-24). The cut keeps per-session text only for the sessions renderStatus reads text from (open, last unwritten, the lane's recent, overlapping write-backs); every other session keeps only what counts, existence and order need. Decision text is kept only for the recent five, the standing rules and the rejected list. TS and Rust change together and write byte-identical files. A v1 file is a key mismatch: it refolds once and rewrites as v2, and v1 files are left for older engines. Re-measure afterwards and stop before D-a, L3 or a render item.
payload.over: D-a, a typed Rust reader (a second copy of 14 from_json acceptance rules, medium risk); L3, sharding the registrations (now ≤3 ms of gain); stopping 4.4 at ~32 ms warm session-start
payload.rule: The digest cut must render byte-identically to the full state: digest-state parity over real logs, team100 and the options matrix gates every change to what the cut keeps.
